item.title: Lee: "Core Industry Investments Must Benefit Both Capital Region and Provinces" (李 “핵심산업 투자, 수도권·지방 윈윈해야”)
item.description:
Lee: "Core Industry Investments Must Benefit Both Capital Region and Provinces" (李 “핵심산업 투자, 수도권·지방 윈윈해야” )

President Lee Jae-myung stated on the 25th, "To overcome the single-pole system centered on the capital region, it is essential to implement a groundbreaking multi-polarization strategy for key industries, expanding large-scale investments in advanced core industries to regions such as Yeongnam, Chungcheong, Gangwon, Jeju, and Honam." This appears to refer to investments like semiconductor projects in Honam. (이재명 대통령은 25일 “수도권 일극 체제 극복을 위해 첨단 핵심 산업에 대한 대규모 투자를 영남이나 충청, 강원, 제주, 호남 등으로 확대하는 획기적인 전략 산업 다극화가 필수적”이라고 밝혔다. 호남 반도체 투자 등을 의미하는 것으로 보인다.)

President Lee made these remarks while chairing a meeting of senior secretaries and aides at the presidential office, saying, "The phenomenal growth effects of some industries have not spread to the provinces, which account for 90% of the national territory, and from the perspective of national and balanced development, the gap in inequality could deepen significantly." (이 대통령은 이날 청와대에서 수석·보좌관 회의를 주재하며 “일부 산업의 경이적인 성장 효과가 국토의 90%를 차지하는 지방까지는 확산하지를 못해서, 국토 발전, 균형 발전이라는 측면에서는 불균등의 골이 훨씬 심화될 수 있다”며 이같이 말했다.)

President Lee added, "If we fail to overcome the single-pole system of the capital region, the good typhoon of change we are currently experiencing could fade into a momentary breeze, or in the worst case, transform into a storm of crisis beyond imagination. We must advance the core infrastructure of the capital region while simultaneously building new industrial and economic bases across the provinces, ensuring a win-win situation for both the capital region and the provinces, and ushering in an era of shared growth for all." (이 대통령은 “수도권 일극 체제를 극복하지 못하면 지금 우리가 경험하고 있는 이 좋은 변화의 태풍은 한순간의 미풍으로 그칠 수 있고, 자칫하면 상상조차 하기 어려운 위기의 폭풍으로 변할 수도 있다”며 “수도권의 핵심 인프라는 그것대로 고도화해 나가고, 동시에 지방 곳곳에 새로운 산업 경제 기반을 구축해 수도권과 지방이 함께 ‘윈윈’하는 모두의 성장 시대를 반드시 열어가야 한다”고 했다.)

President Lee further noted, "A detailed blueprint on this matter will be presented to the people soon." (이 대통령은 “이에 관한 구체적 청사진을 곧 국민 여러분께 보고드릴 예정”이라고 덧붙였다.)

item.title: People Power Party: "Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Powers—Rampaging with Only the 'Cult-like Hardcore Female Supporters' in Sight" (野 “보완수사권 폐지, ‘개딸’만 보고 폭주하는 것”)
item.description:
People Power Party: "Abolition of Supplementary Investigation Powers—Rampaging with Only the 'Cult-like Hardcore Female Supporters' in Sight" (野 “보완수사권 폐지, ‘개딸’만 보고 폭주하는 것”)

On the 25th, the People Power Party criticized Prime Minister Kim Min-seok's announcement of the government's official position to abolish the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers, stating, "The Democratic Party, which is ramping up with only President Lee Jae-myung's hardcore supporters in sight, is ruining the country." <<> Choi Eun-seok, the chief deputy spokesperson of the People Power Party, said in a commentary that day, "Prime Minister Kim has formalized the government's policy to completely abolish the prosecutor's supplementary investigation powers without exception," adding, "Though I had a sliver of doubt, it ultimately ended in the most concerning direction." <<> Chief Deputy Spokesperson Choi stated, "President Lee Jae-myung mentioned the need for supplementary investigations in his 100-day press conference, saying, 'Just because you hate maggots, would you discard the entire soy sauce jar?'" He continued, "Nevertheless, Democratic Party leader Jeong Cheong-rae pushed for the complete abolition of supplementary investigation powers without exception, and Prime Minister Kim formalized that hardline stance as the government's final policy." <<> He then questioned, "Was President Lee's cautious approach ignored? Or was it just empty words from the start? Is it that he preached caution in front of the public while tolerating Representative Jeong Cheong-rae's hardline approach behind the scenes?" <<> Chief Deputy Spokesperson Choi said, "What the government ultimately chose was Representative Jeong's hardline stance, backed by the hardcore female supporters. The Democratic Party is ramping up, looking only for applause from its hardcore supporters, not the Korean people. Is the race for party leadership more important than the Republic of Korea's criminal justice system?" <<> He added, "Politics that shakes the nation's criminal justice system just to earn applause from hardcore supporters is never reform," and urged, "The Democratic Party should face the fact that what is collapsing now is not the prosecution but the fundamental rights that the people should rightfully enjoy." <<> People Power Party lawmaker Joo Jin-woo also wrote on Facebook that day, "The Republic of Korea's public safety has collapsed due to the Democratic Party's hardcore leadership race," and said, "Prime Minister Kim ultimately took a stance to abolish the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers because he must watch the hardcore supporters in the leadership race against Representative Jeong." (국민의힘은 25일 김민석 국무총리가 ‘검찰 보완수사권 폐지’로 정부 입장을 확정 발표한 것에 대해 “개딸(이재명 대통령 강성 지지층)만 보고 폭주하는 더불어민주당이 나라를 망치고 있다”고 했다.)

item.title: Ruling and Opposition Clash Over Han Deok-soo’s Multiple Homes, ‘Everyone’s Startup’, and ‘Main Enemy’ at Hearing (여야, 한성숙 청문회서 다주택·모두의창업·주적 놓고 격돌)
item.description:
Ruling and Opposition Clash Over Han Deok-soo’s Multiple Homes, ‘Everyone’s Startup’, and ‘Main Enemy’ at Hearing (여야, 한성숙 청문회서 다주택·모두의창업·주적 놓고 격돌)

On the first day of the confirmation hearing for Prime Minister nominee Han Deok-soo on the 25th, the ruling and opposition parties clashed over controversies including Han’s multiple home ownership and the personal information leak from the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ ‘Everyone’s Startup’ project. <<> The People Power Party attacked nominee Han for selling his own home ahead of the confirmation hearing, calling it a “transparently calculated move,” given he had previously owned four homes. Lawmaker Kim Sun-kyo said, “Do you recall President Lee Jae-myung using terms like ‘demon’ to vilify multiple homeowners as a social evil? You may have escaped being a ‘demon multiple homeowner’ by the president’s standards, but in the eyes of the public, you seem intoxicated by the power of your position. You’ve merely become a ‘power demon’ stripped of even basic conscience.” <<> In response, nominee Han stated, “I am well aware that the public’s expectations differ between when I was in the private sector and when I am in public office. Selling at a significantly reduced price this time was my way of considering what I could do best after being nominated as Prime Minister.” <<> Lawmaker Kim Hee-jung pointed out that during his confirmation hearing for Minister of SMEs and Startups, Han had promised to quickly resolve suspicions over an illegal extension of a building in Jongno-gu, but sat on the Jongno-gu office’s corrective order for a year. “Is ‘prompt handling’ supposed to take a year and only happen after you’re nominated as Prime Minister?” she asked. On the alleged violation of the Farmland Act regarding land in Yangpyeong, she added, “You were notified by Yangpyeong County that it was a violation—why did you ignore it?” <<> Lawmaker Yoo Young-ha raised the personal information leak from the ‘Everyone’s Startup’ project conducted under Han’s tenure as minister of SMEs, saying, “Suspicions arose that a government minister covered up poor management due to hacking, and controversy over inadequate countermeasures followed. If you receive a pardon with a morning commute apology and become Prime Minister, will the public accept that?” <<> In contrast, the Democratic Party of Korea defended nominee Han. Lawmaker Kim Dong-ah stated that a check with the Korea Post confirmed that Yangpyeong County had not sent any official document to Han, saying, “Claiming such things without properly verifying the facts is truly wrong.” Regarding Han, she said, “He is someone who helped nurture our country’s first-generation venture companies into global big tech firms, and as a female entrepreneur, she broke the glass ceiling in a male-dominated society, serving as a great role model for women.” <<> Lawmaker Baek Seung-ah acknowledged that the ‘Everyone’s Startup’ project should have paid more attention to personal information protection, but added, “I believe he significantly contributed to improving public awareness of startups as a minister, and the ‘Everyone’s Startup’ project was part of that effort, achieving a record number of applications among government startup idea contests.” <<> Lawmaker Kim Han-gyu also emphasized, “In a situation where the government needs to work toward an AI-driven transformation and enrich people’s lives through AI, nominee Han has the experience and capability that both the president and the public can trust.” <<> Meanwhile, a minor incident occurred at the hearing when nominee Han initially referred to the Korean War as “obviously a northern invasion,” but quickly corrected himself, saying, “I’m sorry. It’s a southern invasion. I was nervous.” The People Power Party responded, “The nominee lacks expertise in national defense.” In contrast, Democratic Party lawmaker Park Sun-won countered, “If South-North relations develop to the point of prime ministerial talks, it’s inappropriate to casually mention ‘main enemies’ as if it’s a joke.” (여야는 한성숙 국무총리 후보자에 대한 인사청문회 첫날인 25일 한 후보자의 다주택 논란, 중소벤처기업부 ‘모두의 창업’ 프로젝트 개인 정보 유출 사고 등을 놓고 공방을 벌였다.)

item.title: Han Sung-sook Asked “Where Is the Main Enemy?”: “North Korea Is Both a Threat and a Fellow National” (한성숙, ‘주적 어디냐’ 물음에 “北은 위협이자 동포”)
item.description:
Han Sung-sook Asked “Where Is the Main Enemy?”: “North Korea Is Both a Threat and a Fellow National” (한성숙, ‘주적 어디냐’ 물음에 “北은 위협이자 동포”)

At the parliamentary confirmation hearing for Prime Minister nominee Han Sung-sook held on the 25th, the 76th anniversary of the outbreak of the Korean War, the term “main enemy” became a point of contention. When asked “Where is our main enemy?” Han did not specifically identify the North Korean regime, stating, “Anywhere that threatens the Republic of Korea is our enemy.” Han initially answered that the Korean War was a “northern invasion” but corrected it to “southern invasion,” explaining she was “nervous.” Lawmakers from the People Power Party criticized Han, saying, “She seems to not even properly understand the concept of the main enemy.” Democratic Party of Korea lawmakers argued, “Han is not a candidate for Minister of National Defense,” and that “bringing up the main enemy is inappropriate.” Some also claimed that former President Yoon Suk-yeol is the real main enemy. (6·25전쟁 발발 76주년인 25일 국회에서 열린 한성숙 국무총리 후보자 인사청문회에서는 ‘주적(主敵)’ 용어가 쟁점이 됐다. 한 후보자는 “우리의 주적이 어디냐”는 물음에 북한 정권을 특정하지 않고 “대한민국을 위협하는 곳은 다 우리의 적”이라고 말했다. 한 후보자는 “6·25전쟁은 북침”이라고 답했다가 “남침”이라고 정정하고 “긴장했다”고 해명하기도 했다. 국민의힘 의원들은 “한 후보자가 주적의 개념도 정확히 모르는 것 같다”고 비판했다. 더불어민주당 의원들은 “한 후보자는 국방부 장관 후보자가 아니다”라며 “주적 운운하는 것은 적절치 않다”고 했다. 주적은 윤석열 전 대통령이라는 주장도 나왔다.)

At the first day of the hearing, lawmakers from the People Power Party repeatedly questioned Han about her views on North Korea. This was because Han did not give a clear answer when asked, “Is North Korea our main enemy?” When People Power Party lawmaker Kim Sun-gyo asked, “Where is our main enemy?” Han replied, “North Korea is both a threat and a fellow national—a dual situation,” and during the subsequent Q&A, she made the slip of calling the Korean War a “northern invasion.” (이날 열린 1일 차 청문회에서는 한 후보자의 대북관에 관한 국민의힘 의원들의 질의가 잇따랐다. “북한이 우리의 주적이 맞느냐”는 물음에 한 후보자가 확답하지 않았기 때문이다. 국민의힘 김선교 의원이 “우리의 주적이 어디냐”고 묻자 한 후보자는 “북한은 위협이기도 하고 동포이기도 한 이중적인 상황”이라고 했고, 이어진 질의응답에서 ‘6·25전쟁은 북침’이라는 실언이 나왔다.)

Kim Sun-gyo, People Power Party lawmaker Before the main questioning, I’d like to briefly ask about the candidate’s view of the state and historical awareness. Where is our main enemy? Candidate. (김선교 국민의힘 의원 본질의에 앞서 국무총리 후보자에 대한 국가관과 역사 인식을 간단히 여쭤보고 시작하겠습니다. 우리 주적이 어디입니까? 후보자님.)

Han Sung-sook, Prime Minister nominee I believe that for the Republic of Korea, anywhere that threatens the Republic of Korea is our enemy. (한성숙 국무총리 후보자 저는 대한민국에는, 저희 대한민국을 위협하는 곳들은 다 우리의 적이라고 생각합니다.)

Lawmaker Kim Let me ask more simply. Is North Korea our main enemy? (김 의원 좀 더 간단히 묻겠습니다. 북한이 우리 주적입니까?)

Candidate Han North Korea is both a threat and a fellow national—a very dual situation—so for peace on the Korean Peninsula, I think we need to carefully manage our relationship with them. (한 후보자 북한은 위협이기도 하고 그리고 동포이기도 한 굉장히 이중적인 상황이기 때문에, 한반도 평화를 위해서는 어떻게 잘 관리하, 저희가 잘 관계를 맺고 그리고 관리해야 될 것인가라고 생각합니다.)

Lawmaker Kim To put it more simply, was the Korean War a southern invasion or a northern invasion? (김 의원 더 간단히 들어가서, 6·25가 남침입니까, 북침입니까?)

Candidate Han Oh, that’s a northern invasion. Madam, of course on that part— (한 후보자 아, 그건 북침입니다. 의원님 당연히 그 부분에 대해서)

Lawmaker Kim Pardon? What? (김 의원 예? 뭐요?)

Candidate Han Oh, I’m sorry. It’s a southern invasion. (한 후보자 아, 죄송합니다. 남침입니다.)

Lawmaker Kim That’s why I’m asking. (김 의원 그래서 여쭤보는 거예요.)

Candidate Han Yes, I’m sorry. This is— (한 후보자 네, 죄송합니다. 이건)

Lawmaker Kim Yes, I’ll move on to the next question. (김 의원 예, 다음 질문 가겠습니다.)

Candidate Han I was nervous. Yes. (한 후보자 긴장했습니다. 네.)

People Power Party lawmaker Kim Hee-jung asked Han, “Do you accurately know the concept of the main enemy?” When Han answered, “The enemy that threatens us is the main enemy,” Kim explained, “That’s the general concept of an enemy, and the main enemy is the primary one posing a military threat.” She added, “If you become prime minister, you’ll also be responsible for national defense, but you seem unable to distinguish between the concepts of enemy and main enemy.” When Kim stated, “The North Korean military and the North Korean regime are our main enemy,” Han replied, “I’ll keep your words in mind and listen well.” (국민의힘 김희정 의원은 한 후보자에게 “주적의 개념을 정확하게 알고 있느냐”고 물었다. 한 후보자가 “우리에게 위협이 되는 적이 주적”이라고 답하자, 김 의원은 “그것은 일반적인 적의 개념이고, 군사적 위협이 되는 가장 주된 적이 주적”이라고 설명했다. 그러면서 “총리가 된다면 국방까지 책임져야 하는데, 적과 주적 개념을 구분하지 못하는 것 같다”고 했다. 김 의원이 “북한군과 북한 정권이 우리의 주적”이라고 하자 한 후보자는 “말씀하신 부분을 유념해서 잘 듣겠다”고 했다.)

Kim Hee-jung, People Power Party lawmaker Today is June 25. Since your earlier answer on the main enemy was insufficient, I’ll continue questioning. Do you accurately know the concept of the main enemy? (김희정 국민의힘 의원 오늘이 6월 25일이네요. 그런데 앞서 주적 관련된 답변에 미흡한 점이 있어서 계속 질의 드리겠습니다. 주적의 개념을 정확하게 알고 계십니까?)

Candidate Han I think the main enemy is what threatens us. (한 후보자 우리에게 위협이 되는 것을 주적이라고 생각합니다.)

Lawmaker Kim That’s the general concept of an enemy. What is the main enemy? (김 의원 그거는 일반적인 적 개념입니다. 주적은 무엇입니까?)

Candidate Han Are you referring to the primary enemy? (한 후보자 주된 적을 말씀하시는 건가요?)

Lawmaker Kim Yes. The main enemy is strategically defined as the primary military threat. If you are confirmed as prime minister, you’ll be responsible for national defense, and you seem unable to distinguish between the general concept of an enemy and the military term ‘main enemy,’ so I’m pointing this out. (김 의원 네. 군사적 위협이 되는 가장 주된 적을 전략적인 용어로서 주적으로 명시하고 있습니다. 앞으로 총리에 통과된다면 국방까지 책임지셔야 되는데, 일반적인 적의 개념과 군사적 용어인 주적 개념을 구분을 못 하고 계신 것 같아서 말씀드렸습니다.)

Candidate Han Yes, thank you. (한 후보자 네, 감사합니다.)

Lawmaker Kim Then who is the main enemy of the Republic of Korea? (김 의원 그러면 대한민국의 주적은 누구입니까?)

Candidate Han As you mentioned earlier, the Defense White Paper... (한 후보자 지금 아까 말씀 주신 것처럼 국방백서)

Lawmaker Kim Your previous answer was about the general enemy. (김 의원 아까 답은 일반적인 적으로 답을 하셨습니다.)

Candidate Han Yes, I— (한 후보자 네, 저는)

Lawmaker Kim Who is the main enemy specified in the Republic of Korea’s Defense White Paper? (김 의원 대한민국 국방백서에 명시된 주적은 누구입니까?)

Candidate Han Yes, as I said earlier, North Korea, which threatens us, is an enemy that threatens us, but also a fellow national, and on that part, I think there’s an aspect of how to manage it for peace on the Korean Peninsula. (한 후보자 네, 지금 현재 아까 말씀드렸던 것처럼 우리에게 위협이 되는 북한은 우리에게 위협이 되는 적이기도 하고, 다만 동포이기도 해서, 그 부분에 대해서는 어떻게 잘 한반도 평화를 위해 관리할 거냐라고 하는 부분이 있다고 생각합니다.)

Lawmaker Kim You still don’t know the concept of the main enemy. It specifies the North Korean regime and the North Korean military as the main enemy. Seeing you mix it with the concept of North Korean fellow nationals, you still seem unaware of the concept. Do you understand now? (김 의원 아직도 주적 개념을 모르시는군요. 주적은 북한 정권과 북한군이라고 명시하고 있습니다. 북한 동포와 혼용해서 개념을 쓰고 있는 것 보면 아직도 주적 개념을 모르시는 것 같은데, 이제 이해가 되셨습니까?)

Candidate Han Yes, I will learn well going forward. (한 후보자 네, 앞으로 잘 배우겠습니다.)

Lawmaker Kim Yes, the North Korean military and the North Korean regime are our main enemy. Can you say that again? (김 의원 네, 북한군과 북한 정권이 우리의 주적입니다. 다시 한번 말씀해 주실 수 있겠습니까?)

Candidate Han Yes, I’ll keep the part you mentioned well in mind and listen carefully going forward. (한 후보자 네, 의원님 말씀 주신 부분 잘 유념해서 앞으로 잘 듣도록 하겠습니다.)

Lawmaker Kim You’re trying not to say it yourself to the end. Keep in mind that the fallen patriots and war heroes are listening to your answers today. (김 의원 끝까지 자기 입으로 얘기 안 하려고 하네요. 오늘 순국선열과 호국영령들이 당신의 답을 듣고 있다는 거 명심하시기 바랍니다.)

Candidate Han Yes. (한 후보자 네.)

In contrast, Democratic Party of Korea lawmaker Park Sun-won argued that asking Han where the main enemy is, is itself inappropriate. Park said, “Han is someone who could potentially hold prime ministerial talks with North Korea if inter-Korean relations develop,” and added, “Bringing up this ‘main enemy’ talk, which young people use as a joke, is not appropriate for such a person.” (반면 더불어민주당 박선원 의원은 한 후보자에게 주적이 어디인지를 묻는 것 자체가 적절하지 않다고 주장했다. 박 의원은 “한 후보자는 남북 관계가 발전되면 (북한과) 총리 회담을 할 수도 있는 분”이라며 “그런 분에게 젊은 층이 농담처럼 한다는 주적 운운하는 것은 적절치 않다”고 했다.)

Park Sun-won, Democratic Party of Korea lawmaker I visited a country with a security environment similar to ours and asked, ‘How do you use the term main enemy and how do you mark it in official documents?’ They said ‘main enemy.’ Do you know what they replied? They said, ‘Is there such a foolish and stupid country in the world? Why would you write the main enemy in your defense white paper or national defense report? What country is so foolish in its security policy?’ they said. (박선원 더불어민주당 의원 제가 우리나라와 비슷한 안보 환경에 처한 나라에 방문을 해가지고, ‘당신들은 주적을 어떻게 쓰고 공식 문서에 어떻게 표시하느냐’라고 물었어요. ‘main enemy’라고 했어요. 그랬더니 뭐라고 대답한 줄 아십니까? ‘세상에 그렇게 멍청하고 어리석은 나라가 있느냐? 자신의 방위백서나 국방 보고서에 주적, 그걸 왜 쓰냐? 그렇게 어리석게 안보 정책을 하는 나라가 어디 있느냐’ 그렇게 이야기를 하더라고요.)

Our Republic of Korea already has our strategic resource deployments, missile directions, major radar transmission devices, their locations, and reconnaissance and intelligence satellites, using joint ROK-U.S. forces—reconnaissance mission targets are all set. (이미 우리 대한민국은 우리의 전략 자원 배치, 미사일의 방향, 주요 레이더 발신 장치, 그 위치 그리고 정보 위성, 첩보 위성, 한·미 연합 전력을 공동으로 사용해서 정찰 임무 대상 다 정해져 있습니다.)

You’re not a candidate for Minister of National Defense; you’re a candidate for Prime Minister. And if inter-Korean relations develop, you could hold prime ministerial talks. For such a person, I think it’s inappropriate to bring up this ‘main enemy’ talk that young people use as a joke these days. (국방장관 후보자가 아니십니다, 국무총리 후보자는. 또 남북 관계가 발전되면 총리 회담도 할 수 있는 분입니다. 그런 분에게 요새 젊은 층이 그렇게 농담처럼 한다는 주적 운운한다는 것에 대해서는 저는 적절치 않다, 이렇게 생각합니다.)

Independent lawmaker Choi Hye-jin, who has applied to rejoin the Democratic Party, argued, “The concept of the main enemy itself has become an outdated way of thinking.” He further claimed that those involved in the December 3 martial law—including former President Yoon Suk-yeol—and the person who attacked then-Democratic Party leader Lee at the Busan Gadeokdo New Airport site in January 2024 with a weapon are the main enemies. (민주당에 복당을 신청한 최혁진 무소속 의원은 “주적이라는 개념 자체가 구시대적인 사고가 됐다”고 주장했다. 그러면서 윤석열 전 대통령 등 12·3 비상 계엄에 연루된 사람들과 2024년 1월 부산 가덕도신공항 부지에서 당시 민주당 대표였던 이 대통령을 흉기로 공격한 사람이 주적이라고 주장했다.)

Choi Hye-jin, Independent lawmaker I had prepared other questions, but since talk of the main enemy keeps coming up because today is June 25, I’ll briefly address that and then proceed with my questioning. (최혁진 무소속 의원 제가 이제 다른 질의를 준비했는데, 우선 갑자기 앞에서 오늘 6·25이기 때문에 주적에 대한 얘기가 자꾸 나와서, 그 부분을 잠깐 말씀드리고 저의 또 질의로 진행하도록 하겠습니다.)

Earlier, the esteemed member Park Sun-won said that globally, the concept of the main enemy itself has become a very outdated way of thinking, and I agree with that. The perspective on security itself has changed recently. Security studies have changed too. If security in the past was about a system to prepare against an opponent that could provoke war, now it’s about a system to prepare against entities that can threaten the lives and safety of the people. Naturally, how we view the main enemy should also be reinterpreted from the perspective of who is threatening the lives and safety of the people in the current era and what preparation system we have for that. I think the concept of the main enemy that the People Power Party members speak of probably includes those aspects too. (그 아까 존경하는 박선원 위원님께서 이제 전 세계적으로 주적이라는 개념 자체는 굉장히 구시대적인 사고가 됐다라고 하는 것에 대해서 저도 동의를 합니다. 최근에 안보라고 하는 관점 자체가 다 바뀌었습니다. 안보학도 바뀌었습니다. 안보라고 하는 것 자체가 과거에는 전쟁을 유발할 수 있는 상대에 대한 대비 체제라고 했다면, 지금은 국민의 생명과 안전을 위협할 수 있는 존재에 대한 대비 체계를 안보라고 얘기합니다. 당연히 이제 주적이라고 바라보는 것도 현 시기에 국민의 생명과 안전을 누가 위협하고 있는가, 그것에 대해서 우리가 어떤 대비 체계를 하는가, 그런 관점으로 새롭게 해석돼야 된다고 보고 있고, 아마 국민의힘 위원들께서 말씀하시는 주적 개념도 그런 부분들을 포함할 것이라고 생각합니다.)

Today we’re talking about North Korea, but we don’t treat them with hostility just because they have a socialist system, right? We engage in economic trade and political exchanges with Vietnam. We also exchange with China. We respond strongly to North Korea only because of the indelible wounds inflicted on the people of the Republic of Korea through their southern invasion during the Korean War. From a recent security perspective, if we were to use the concept of a main enemy—and it’s not appropriate to use it anyway—who would it be? (오늘 북한 얘기를 하는데, 사실 우리가 사회주의 체제를 가졌다 그래서 우리가 적대시하지는 않지 않습니까? 베트남하고도 우리가 경제 교역도 하고 정치적인 교류들도 하고 있습니다. 중국하고도 교류를 하고 있습니다. 다만 북한이 6·25 때 남침을 통해서 대한민국 국민들에게 씻을 수 없는 상처를 줬다는 이유 때문에 우리가 이렇게 강력하게 대응을 하고 있다고 생각을 하는데요, 저는 이제 최근의 안보 관점으로 보면 주적 개념이라고 하는 걸 굳이 쓴다면, 쓰는 것도 적절치 않지만, 누가 주적이겠습니까?)

Prime Minister, you need to be clear: the main enemies are those who made our children, raised like precious gems, pick up guns and point them at the National Assembly. The main enemies are those who used military force to try to destroy the democratic constitutional order of the Republic of Korea. The main enemies are those who tried to assassinate the opposition leader through terror at the Gadeokdo attack—those who tried to undermine the democratic order of the Republic of Korea. They don’t even repent afterward. (총리님, 분명히 하셔야 되는 것이, 우리가 금지옥엽으로 키운 자식들에게 총을 들려 가지고 국회를 향하게 한 사람들이 주적인 겁니다. 대한민국의 민주 헌정 질서를 군사력을 동원해서 파괴하려고 한 것이 주적입니다. 가덕도 테러에서 야당의 대표를 갖다 테러를 통해서 살해하려고 했던 사람들이, 대한민국의 민주주의 질서를 훼손하려고 했던 사람들이 주적입니다. 심지어 그 이후에 반성도 하지 않습니다.)

I knew this would come up, so I prepared something. Yes, People Power Party lawmakers: ‘The president’s martial law was to save the country.’ ‘It was patriotic loyalty.’ ‘The martial law was to appeal to the people because the country might collapse.’ ‘Executing the arrest warrant for Yoon Suk-yeol is illegal.’ How can those who even sent drones to provoke North Korea keep saying these things? (이런 얘기 나올 줄 알고 제가 하나 만들어 왔습니다. 예, 국민의힘 의원님들, ‘대통령의 계엄은 나라를 살리기 위한 것이다.’ ‘애국 충정이다.’ ‘나라가 망할까 봐 국민에게 호소하기 위한 계엄을 했다.’ ‘윤석열 체포 영장 집행은 불법이다.’ 북한의 도발을 유인하기 위해서 무인기까지 보낸 사람들이 어떻게 이런 이야기를 계속할 수 있습니까?)

So, if you become prime minister, to strengthen the security of the Republic of Korea and for its future prosperity, who is the main enemy? Please be unequivocal: carry out a firm and thorough crackdown on the insurrection forces, and make it clear that on this foundation, the Republic of Korea can move forward as a trusted nation. (그래서, 총리가 되시면 대한민국의 안보를 강화하기 위해서라도, 대한민국의 미래 번영을 위해서라도, 누가 주적인가? 내란 세력에 대한 척결은 단호하고 철저하게 하시고, 그 토대 위에서 대한민국이 신뢰받는 국가로 나아갈 수 있을 것이라는 부분들을 분명히 해 주시기 바랍니다.)

Candidate Han Yes, understood. (한 후보자 네, 알겠습니다.)

item.title: Kim Eo-jun on Lee's Falling Approval Ratings: "Core Support Base Defecting... Performance Alone Won't Fix It" (김어준, 李 지지율 하락에 “코어 지지층 이탈…성과 낸다고 해결 안돼”)
item.description:
Kim Eo-jun on Lee's Falling Approval Ratings: "Core Support Base Defecting... Performance Alone Won't Fix It" (김어준, 李 지지율 하락에 “코어 지지층 이탈…성과 낸다고 해결 안돼”)

Pro-government YouTuber Kim Eo-jun pointed out on the 25th regarding President Lee Jae-myung's declining approval ratings, "Unlike typical declines, the 'core support base' is defecting." (친여 유튜버 김어준씨가 25일 이재명 대통령의 지지율 하락세를 놓고 “통상의 하락과 달리 ‘코어 지지층’이 이탈하고 있다”고 지적했다.)

On his YouTube broadcast that day, Kim said, "President Lee is a politician who has boosted his approval ratings through his own performance since his time as Mayor of Seongnam, and he maintained high ratings even in his first year in office." He added, "Typically, a drop in approval ratings starts with the less loyal peripheral supporters. But now, without any particular incident, the core support base is wavering—an unfamiliar scene is unfolding." (김씨는 이날 자신의 유튜브 방송에서 “이 대통령은 성남시장 시절부터 스스로 성과를 내 지지율을 끌어올린 정치인이고, 임기 1년 차에도 높은 지지율을 만들었다”고 했다. 그는 그러면서 “통상적인 지지율 하락은 충성도가 낮은 외곽 지지층부터 빠지는 법인데, 지금은 특별한 사건이 없음에도 코어 지지층이 흔들리는 생소한 풍경이 펼쳐지고 있다”고 했다.)

Kim noted, "Former President Roh Moo-hyun also struggled throughout his term as his core support base collapsed," and stressed, "This isn't something that can be resolved simply by showing results." He also warned, "The 'decoupling' signal where presidential approval ratings and party approval ratings diverge is very dangerous." (김씨는 “과거 노무현 전 대통령도 코어 지지층이 무너지며 임기 내내 힘들었다”며 “이는 단순히 성과를 보여준다고 해결되는 게 아니다”라고 했다. 또 “대통령 지지율과 정당 지지율이 분리되는 ‘디커플링’ 신호는 매우 위험하다”고도 했다.)

In a broadcast on the 23rd, Kim had said, "This is the first crisis since the launch of the Lee Jae-myung administration. The first major crisis of the Moon Jae-in administration was the 'Chosun Kuk' scandal, and the scale of this drop is comparable to that." He added, "On the surface, there's nothing special, but it's plummeted. The core support base is leaving." (김씨는 지난 23일 방송에서도 “이재명 정부 출범 이후 첫 번째 위기다. 문재인 정부의 첫 번째 큰 위기는 조국 사태였는데 낙폭은 거기에 비견될 정도로 크다”며 “겉으로 보면 특별한 게 없는데 훅 빠졌다. 코어 지지층이 빠진 것”이라고 했다.)

He explained, "The core support base immediately abandons those who reject their identity," and "They haven't turned their backs completely yet, but they've crossed their arms and gone 'Oh my.'" He added, "If left as is, they'll keep their arms crossed and eventually turn away." (그는 “코어 지지층은 자기 정체성을 부정하는 사람들을 바로 버린다”며 “코어 지지층이 등까지는 안 돌렸는데 ‘어머’ 하고 팔짱을 껴버린 것”이라고 했다. 그러면서 “이걸 두면 팔짱을 끼고 있다가 등을 돌린다는 것”이라고 했다.)

item.title: Next UN Secretary-General Candidates Gather on Jeju... United Call for Restoring Trust in the UN (차기 유엔총장 후보들 제주 집결... 유엔 신뢰회복 한목소리)
item.description:
Next UN Secretary-General Candidates Gather on Jeju... United Call for Restoring Trust in the UN (차기 유엔총장 후보들 제주 집결... 유엔 신뢰회복 한목소리)

Candidates for the next UN Secretary-General gathered on Jeju Island on the 25th, collectively emphasizing the need for reform of the UN, which is facing a crisis. (차기 유엔 사무총장 후보들이 25일 제주에 집결해 위기를 맞은 유엔의 개혁을 한목소리로 강조했다.)

At the Jeju Forum session titled "UN Secretary-General Candidates Dialogue" held that day at the Haevichi Hotel on Jeju, five participants took part: former UN General Assembly President María Fernanda Espinosa, International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi, UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) Secretary-General Rebeca Grynspan Mayufis, Guyana's UN Ambassador Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett, and former Senegalese President Macky Sall. Former Chilean President Michelle Bachelet joined via video message due to scheduling reasons. (이날 제주 해비치호텔에서 열린 제주포럼 ‘유엔 사무총장 후보자 대담’ 세션에는 마리아 페르난다 에스피노사 전 유엔총회 의장, 라파엘 마리아노 그로시 국제원자력기구(IAEA) 사무총장, 레베카 그린스판 마유피스 유엔무역개발회의(UNCTAD) 사무총장, 캐롤린 로드리게스-버케트 주유엔가이아나대사, 마키 살 전 세네갈 대통령 등 5명이 참석했다. 미첼 바첼레트 전 칠레 대통령은 일정상 사유로 영상 메시지를 통해 함께했다.)

Former President Espinosa emphasized the importance of being perceived as a "fair mediator" to restore trust in the UN. She also stated that "the UN must act much earlier than it currently does" in dealing with conflicts. Director General Grossi noted that while there are various consultative bodies like the G7, G20, and BRICS, "the UN is the only truly global platform," highlighting the UN's role. Secretary-General Grynspan stressed expanding cooperation with the private sector, saying, "The capabilities of national governments, regional organizations, and the private sector and civil society have expanded compared to the past." (에스피노사 전 의장은 유엔의 신뢰 회복을 위해 ‘공정한 중재자’로 인식되는 것이 중요하다고 했다. 또 분쟁을 대하는 데 있어 “유엔은 지금보다 훨씬 더 일찍 행동해야 한다”고 했다. 그로시 사무총장은 G7(주요 7국)과 G20, 브릭스(BRICS) 등 다양한 협의체가 있지만 “유엔만이 유일하게 진정한 범세계적인 플랫폼”이라며 유엔의 역할을 강조했다. 그린스판 사무총장은 “각국 정부, 지역 기구, 민간과 시민사회의 역량이 과거보다 확대됐다”며 민간 부문과의 협력 확대를 강조했다.)

Former President Sall remarked, "Member states must engage in reform, and the Security Council needs to open up." Ambassador Rodrigues-Birkett stated, "Reform and adjustment cannot be one-time events; they must be ongoing." Former President Bachelet said in her video message, "We need multilateralism that prevents crises before they erupt." (살 전 대통령은 “회원국들이 개혁에 참여해야 하고, 안보리도 개방할 필요가 있다”고 말했다. 로드리게스-버케트 대사는 “개혁과 조정은 일회성이 아니라 지속해 이뤄져야 한다”고 했다. 바첼레트 전 대통령은 영상에서 “위기가 폭발하기 전에 예방하는 다자주의가 필요하다”고 했다.)

Former UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon in his opening speech diagnosed, "The UN is facing a serious financial crisis, and its authority and trust are being challenged," adding, "The next Secretary-General will have a very rare opportunity to restore trust in broken multilateralism and demonstrate that it can change the lives of ordinary people around the world." (반기문 전 유엔 사무총장은 이날 개회사에서 “유엔은 심각한 재정 위기에 직면해있고, 권위와 신뢰는 도전받고 있다”고 진단하면서 “(차기 총장이) 무너진 다자주의에 대한 신뢰를 회복하고, 세계 곳곳 평범한 사람들의 삶을 바꿀 수 있다는 것을 보여주는 매우 드문 기회를 갖게 될 것”이라고 했다.)

In a separate session at the Jeju Forum, former Secretary-General Ban said, "No country can survive alone," urging the United States to return to the Paris Climate Agreement and key international organizations. Regarding the US withdrawal from dozens of international organizations, including UN bodies, he stated, "I ask that you return to international organizations," and emphasized, "We must cooperate and live together with neighboring countries and the international community." (반 전 총장은 제주포럼 별도 세션에선 “어떤 국가도 혼자 살아갈 수는 없다”며 미국을 향해 파리 기후변화 협약과 주요 국제기구 복귀를 촉구했다. 그는 미국이 유엔 기구를 포함해 국제기구 수십 곳에서 탈퇴한 것에 대해 “국제기구로 다시 돌아오기를 부탁드린다”며 “이웃 국가, 국제사회와 함께 협력하고 살아가야 한다”고 했다.)

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that Foreign Minister Cho Tae-yul met individually with five UN Secretary-General candidates on the 24th and 25th on the sidelines of the Jeju Forum to exchange views on the UN's role and cooperation measures for international peace and prosperity. Minister Cho stated, "Amid the international community facing complex crises such as geopolitical conflicts, climate change, and the advancement of new technologies, it is important to build a UN that effectively responds to these challenges and earns the trust of the international community." (조현 외교부 장관은 제주포럼을 계기로 24~25일 유엔 사무총장 후보자 5명과 각각 만나 국제 평화와 번영을 위한 유엔의 역할과 협력 방안 등에 대해 의견을 교환했다고 외교부가 밝혔다. 조 장관은 “국제사회가 지정학적 갈등과 기후변화, 신기술 발전 등으로 복합적 위기에 직면한 가운데, 이에 효과적으로 대응하고 국제사회의 신뢰를 받는 유엔을 구축하는 것이 중요하다”고 했다.)

item.title: Jung Cheong-rae on Kim Min-seok's Announcement of Supplementary Investigation Powers: "Dumped on the National Assembly... Hope It's Not a Trick" (정청래, 보완수사권 김민석 발표에 “국회로 떠넘겨... 꼼수 아니길”)
item.description:
Jung Cheong-rae on Kim Min-seok's Announcement of Supplementary Investigation Powers: "Dumped on the National Assembly... Hope It's Not a Trick" (정청래, 보완수사권 김민석 발표에 “국회로 떠넘겨... 꼼수 아니길”)

Former Democratic Party of Korea leader Jung Cheong-rae stated on the 25th, regarding Prime Minister Kim Min-seok's announcement that the abolition of supplementary investigation powers would be the government's final position but that the government would not submit a bill to the National Assembly, "The government has dumped (the discussion on abolishing supplementary investigation powers) onto the National Assembly, so now they must answer the question, 'Then let's do it right now.'" (정청래 더불어민주당 전 대표가 25일 보완수사권 폐지를 정부 최종 입장으로 하되 정부안은 국회에 제출하지 않겠다는 김민석 국무총리의 발표에 대해 “(정부가) 국회로 (보완수사권 폐지 논의를) 떠넘겼으니 이제 ‘그럼 지금 당장 하자’에 대한 답을 해야한다”고 말했다.)

Jung made these remarks in a Facebook post that day, saying, "It would have been best if the government bill for the complete abolition of supplementary investigation powers had come to the National Assembly." He added, "We need to check if this is a stalling tactic," and stated, "My answer is, 'Let's do it right now, finish it before Constitution Day.'" (정 전 대표는 이날 페이스북 글을 통해 “정부안으로 ‘보완수사권 전면 폐지’가 국회로 왔으면 제일 좋았을 것”이라며 이같이 언급했다. 그러면서 “혹시 시간 끌기 작전인지 살펴봐야 한다”며 “나의 답은 ‘지금 당장, 제헌절 전에 끝내자’”라고 했다.)

At a workshop for elected officials from North Jeolla Province held in Jeongeup that day, Jung also emphasized, "From now on, we must discuss the revision of the Criminal Procedure Act (for abolishing supplementary investigation powers) and the enforcement decree," and stressed, "We must pass the revision before Constitution Day." (정 전 대표는 이날 전북 정읍에서 열린 전북 당선인 워크숍에서도 “지금부터라도 (보완수사권 폐지를 위한) 형사소송법 개정을 놓고, 또한 시행령을 놓고 고민해야 한다”며 “제헌절 이전에는 (개정안을) 통과시켜야 한다”고 강조하기도 했다.)

He further stated, "Otherwise, the launch of the Prosecution Service Office and the Major Crimes Investigation Office (MCIO) will be physically impossible," and added, "The fact that no progress has been made on the legislation so far is an extremely dangerous situation." (또 “그렇지 않으면 공소청, 중수청(중대범죄수사청) 출범이 물리적으로 불가능하다”며 “지금까지 (법안 마련이) 안됐다는 건 대단히 위험한 상황‘이라고 했다.)

In response, pro-Moon Jae-in lawmaker Lee Geon-tae, a former lawyer from the Daejang-dong case, pushed back, posting on his Facebook page, "It's beyond disappointment; it's shocking. A former leader of the ruling party is talking about the government's official position as a 'stalling tactic.'" (그러자 대장동 변호인 출신 친명 이건태 의원이 반발하며 자신의 페이스북에 “실망을 넘어 충격이다. 여당 대표였던 사람이 정부의 공식입장에 대해 ‘시간끌기’를 운운하다니”라고 했다.)

He then said, "This is no different from doubting the Yoon Suk Yeol government. I miss the Jung Cheong-rae from his days as chairman of the Legislation and Judiciary Committee." (그러면서 이 의원은 “이재명 정부를 의심하는 발언과 다름없다. 법사위원장 시절의 정청래가 그립다”고 했다.)

Following this, Jung again posted on Facebook, saying, "I wonder if we've been wasting time for a year," and "I'm also very curious about what has been prepared over the past year. I pray with both hands that it's not a trick to buy time." (이어 정 전 대표는 또 다시 페이스북에 “1년동안 허송세월을 한 것은 아닌지”라며 “1년동안 준비한 내용이 무엇인지도 참 궁금하다. 시간끌기용 꼼수가 아니길 두 손 모아 기도 한다”라고 했다.)

item.title: One Day After Discharge, Lawmakers Say "Resign Voluntarily"... Calls for a 'Vote of Confidence' Emerge (張 퇴원 하루만에 의원들 “자진 사퇴하라”...‘재신임 투표’ 주장도 나와)
item.description:
One Day After Discharge, Lawmakers Say "Resign Voluntarily"... Calls for a 'Vote of Confidence' Emerge (張 퇴원 하루만에 의원들 “자진 사퇴하라”...‘재신임 투표’ 주장도 나와)

A day after People Power Party (PPP) leader Jang Dong-hyuk was discharged from the hospital, on the 25th, demands for his resignation erupted again within the PPP. The previous day, Chairman Jang dismissed the issue of his own position, stating, "It's a matter for the party members to decide," and within the party, there were even claims that a 'vote of confidence' should be held for Chairman Jang. (국민의힘 장동혁 대표가 퇴원한 지 하루 만인 25일 국민의힘에선 당대표 사퇴 요구가 또다시 분출했다. 전날 장 대표가 “당원들이 결정할 문제”라며 자신의 거취 문제를 일축하자, 당내에선 장 대표에 대한 ‘재신임 투표’를 해야 한다는 주장까지 나왔다.)

The 'Alternative and Future' group, a core gathering of first and second-term lawmakers within the PPP, held a breakfast meeting that morning at the National Assembly Members' Office Building and agreed to "urge Chairman Jang to voluntarily resign for the sake of the party's future," according to Rep. Lee Seong-kwon, the group's secretary. Rep. Lee stated, "There can be no trust without faith; with a leadership that has lost trust, the party's future cannot be expected." (국민의힘 초·재선 중심 모임인 ‘대안과 미래’는 이날 오전 국회 의원회관에서 조찬 회동을 열고 “당의 미래를 위해 장 대표가 스스로 사퇴할 것을 촉구한다”고 의견을 모았다고 모임 간사인 이성권 의원이 밝혔다. 이 의원은 “무신불립(無信不立), 신뢰 잃은 리더십으로는 당의 미래를 기대할 수 없다”고 했다.)

Rep. Lee further urged, "I call on the elected supreme council members, including Supreme Council member Shin Dong-wook, to make a decision." Since Chairman Jang has clearly drawn a line against resignation calls, this was interpreted as a call for the entire leadership, including supreme council members, to resign collectively, dissolve the supreme council, and elect a new leadership through a party convention. (이 의원은 이어 “신동욱 최고위원을 비롯한 선출직 최고위원들의 결단을 촉구한다”고 했다. 장 대표는 사퇴론에 선을 분명히 그었으니, 최고위원 등 지도부가 총사퇴해 최고위를 해산하고 전당대회를 통해 새 지도부를 선출하자는 뜻으로 해석됐다.)

At the meeting that day, there were also reports of voices advocating for pushing a 'vote of confidence for the party leader' among all party members. However, it was said that no conclusion was reached as some lawmakers dissuaded, saying, "If we initiate a vote of confidence right now, it will place a heavy burden on floor leader Jeong Jeom-sik, who is gathering opinions to manage the situation." One senior lawmaker commented, "Pushing Chairman Jang too hard now could intensify internal strife. We need to manage the pace." (이날 모임에선 아예 전 당원을 대상으로 한 ‘당대표 재신임 투표’를 추진해야 한다는 목소리도 나온 것으로 전해졌다. 다만 일부 의원이 “지금 당장 재신임 투표를 띄우면 사태 수습을 위해 의견을 수렴 중인 정점식 원내대표에게 큰 부담이 될 것”이라고 만류하면서 결론을 내지는 않았다고 한다. 한 중진 의원은 “지금 장 대표를 몰아붙이면 내분이 격화할 가능성이 크다”며 “속도 조절이 필요하다”고 했다.)

Regarding Chairman Jang's re-emphasis on the previous day about the need for a 'by-election' in connection with the shortage of ballots for the June 3 local elections, the lawmakers' meeting stated, "It constitutes an act of insubordination for the party leader to reject a conclusion already reached at the general meeting of lawmakers." Earlier, on the 17th, the PPP had decided at a general meeting to pursue an election appeal only for areas where the ballot shortage was confirmed. Rep. Lee Seong-kwon said, "Let's convene a general meeting of lawmakers including the party leader and gather consensus again through a secret ballot," and requested floor leader Jeong, "Please ensure that the party leader no longer makes individual statements that plunge the party into chaos." (의원 모임은 장 대표가 전날 6·3 지방선거 투표용지 부족 사태와 관련해 ‘재선거’ 필요성을 재차 강조한 것에 대해선 “이미 의원총회에서 결론이 난 것을 당 대표가 거부하는 건 해당 행위”라고 했다. 앞서 국민의힘은 지난 17일 의총에서 투표용지 부족 사태가 확인된 일부 지역에 한해서만 선거소청을 추진키로 했다. 이성권 의원은 “당 대표를 포함한 의총을 열고 비밀투표를 통해 총의를 (다시) 모으자”며 “당 대표가 더 이상 개인 의견을 발표해 당을 혼란에 빠뜨리지 않도록 해달라”고 정 원내대표에게 요청했다.)

At the supreme council meeting that day, which Chairman Jang chaired for the first time since returning to party duties, he urged an immediate acceptance of a special counsel regarding the ballot shortage, saying, "Rejecting a special counsel will be the fuse that sinks the administration." He made no comments on internal party issues, including his own position. A party insider remarked, "Since he has already made his stance clear on the resignation demands, this likely means he intends to focus on attacking the opposition." (장 대표는 당무 복귀 후 처음 주재한 이날 최고위원 회의에서 투표용지 부족 사태와 관련해 “특검 거부는 정권 침몰의 도화선이 될 것”이라며 즉각 특검을 수용하라고 촉구했다. 자신의 거취를 비롯한 당내 문제와 관련해선 발언하지 않았다. 야당 관계자는 “사퇴 요구에 대해선 이미 입장을 명확히 했으니 대여 공세에 집중하겠다는 뜻 아니겠냐”고 했다.)

item.title: US Deputy Secretary of State: "Looking Forward to Collaboration with Korea, Home to the World's Top Semiconductor Makers" (美국무차관 “세계 최고 반도체 메이커 있는 한국과 협력 기대”)
item.description:
US Deputy Secretary of State: "Looking Forward to Collaboration with Korea, Home to the World's Top Semiconductor Makers" (美국무차관 “세계 최고 반도체 메이커 있는 한국과 협력 기대”)

Jacob Helberg, U.S. Deputy Secretary of State for Energy and Economic Growth, stated on the 25th, "Korea has some of the world's best chipmakers," adding, "We have held regular bilateral dialogues with Korea, and we are very pleased to be able to continuously deepen our collaboration with Korea." Helberg made these remarks while meeting with reporters at the 'Pax Silica' summit held at the Donald J. Trump Peace Institute in Washington, D.C. that morning. Amid a global shortage of infrastructure, such as data centers, needed to support the AI era, Helberg also noted, "I am curious about the opinions of Korean companies." <<> Launched in December of last year, Pax Silica is a multilateral AI supply chain consultative body that the Trump administration is championing amid its hegemonic competition with China. Although it does not explicitly single out China, its top priority is to build supply chains among "trustworthy nations." When it was first launched last year, only seven countries, including South Korea and Japan, were members, but since then, Greece, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and the Philippines have sequentially joined. Furthermore, with this year's second summit, the European Union (EU), Kazakhstan, Costa Rica, Chile, and Argentina have also participated, expanding the membership to around 20 countries. The U.S. views South Korea as a key partner in the AI supply chain, and at the scene that day, numerous Korean officials attended, including Second Vice Foreign Minister Kim Jin-a, as well as representatives from Korean companies like Korea Zinc. South Korea also serves as the chair of 'FORGE' (Forum on Geostrategic Resources), a critical minerals bloc led by the U.S. <<> In his speech that day, Helberg stated, "Pax Silica has grown into a coalition representing over 30 governments and economic zones, including observer countries," adding, "This reflects a shared recognition that AI will shape not only the future of technology but also the future of economic growth, competitiveness, and prosperity." He further noted, "If the 20th century was driven by oil and steel, the 21st century will be driven by computing, energy, and AI ecosystem infrastructure," and emphasized, "Inefficiencies in the movement of goods, talent shortages, infrastructure investment gaps, and unnecessary barriers to innovation are problems no single country can solve alone. They can only be addressed when trusted partners come together, which is why Pax Silica exists." <<> On the occasion of this meeting, member countries are expected to adopt an 'AI Opportunity Declaration,' expressing their commitment to growth-oriented AI policies, a trusted technology ecosystem, resilient supply chains, and infrastructure investment needed to support the AI economy. Helberg, who comes from Palantir and is well-versed in the tech industry, said, "Governments should approach AI from an opportunity perspective, not a regulatory one." He also announced the launch of the 'Foundry School,' a workforce development initiative in collaboration with Stanford University to cultivate entrepreneurs, engineers, and leaders in advanced manufacturing across the Pax Silica economic sphere. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau stated, "We did not want a world where every supply chain becomes a tool of pressure, and every dependency becomes a potential weapon," and concluded, "The answer lies in trusted partners coming together to build a new economic order." (제이콥 헬버그 미 국무부 에너지·경제 성장 담당 차관은 25일 “한국에는 세계 최고 수준의 반도체 메이커(chipmaker)들이 있다”며 “우리는 한국과 정기적으로 양자(兩者) 간 대화를 나눠왔고 한국과 협력을 지속적으로 심화해 나갈 수 있게 돼 매우 기쁘다”고 했다. 헬버그는 이날 오전 워싱턴 DC의 도널드 J. 트럼프 평화연구소에서 열린 ‘팍스 실리카(Pax Silica)’ 정상회의 현장에서 기자들과 만나 이같이 밝혔다. 데이터 센터 같이 인공지능(AI) 시대를 뒷받침할 인프라 부족 문제가 세계적으로 대두되고 있는 가운데, 헬버그는 “한국 기업들의 의견이 궁금하다”고도 했다.)

item.title: When Asked 'Is North Korea the Main Enemy?', Han Duck-soo Says "Anywhere That Threatens South Korea Is the Enemy" (‘北이 주적인가’ 묻자, 한성숙 “한국 위협하는 곳 모두 적”)
item.description:
When Asked 'Is North Korea the Main Enemy?', Han Duck-soo Says "Anywhere That Threatens South Korea Is the Enemy" (‘北이 주적인가’ 묻자, 한성숙 “한국 위협하는 곳 모두 적”)

At the National Assembly confirmation hearing for Prime Minister nominee Han Duck-soo held on the 25th, questions poured in regarding his views on North Korea and the process of disposing of his real estate. The People Power Party (PPP) probed the diplomatic and security perspectives of Han, a former CEO of Naver who was appointed Minister of SMEs and Startups just a year ago before being nominated as Prime Minister. The Democratic Party of Korea (DP) lauded the sale of three of Han’s four homes ahead of the hearing, stating, "There aren’t many people like this; it deserves high praise." This hearing failed to adopt witnesses and references due to disagreements between the ruling and opposition parties, with the PPP accusing the DP of "undermining the National Assembly’s authority to vet personnel." <<> During the hearing, in response to a question from PPP lawmaker Kim Sun-kyo (Gyeonggi Yeoju-Yangpyeong) asking, "Where is our main enemy?" Han refrained from specifically naming North Korea, saying, "Anywhere that threatens the Republic of Korea is our enemy." When PPP lawmaker Kim Hee-jung (Busan Yeonje) stated, "The North Korean military and regime are our main enemy," Han replied, "I will keep your remarks in mind and listen carefully." When asked whether the Korean War was a "northern invasion" or a "southern invasion," Han initially answered "northern invasion" but corrected it to "southern invasion," adding, "I was nervous." <<> DP lawmaker Park Sun-won (Incheon Bupyeong B) said, "Han is someone who could hold a prime ministerial meeting with North Korea if inter-Korean relations improve. It’s inappropriate to talk about 'main enemies' with such a person." Independent lawmaker Choi Hyuk-jin (Proportional Representation), who applied to rejoin the DP, stated, "The people who armed our cherished children and aimed guns at the National Assembly, or those who tried to assassinate the opposition leader in Gadeokdo, are the Republic of Korea’s true enemies." <<> Lawmakers also continued questioning Han regarding his sale of three of four homes ahead of the confirmation hearing. Han owned a single-family home in Samcheong-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul; an apartment in Jamsil, Songpa-gu, Seoul; an officetel in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam-gu, Seoul; and a single-family home in Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi Province. He sold the Jamsil apartment in May and recently sold the Yeoksam-dong officetel and Yangpyeong home, becoming a single-homeowner. In response, the opposition remarked, "Homes he didn’t sell as a minister, he offloaded to become prime minister." <<> At the hearing, Han expressed regret, saying, "I apologize for holding multiple homes, which does not align with the public’s expectations." DP lawmaker Park Kyun-taek (Gwangju Gwangsan A) noted, "The properties he owned previously do not appear to have been purchased for speculative purposes." DP lawmaker Park Sun-won added, "The fact that he disposed of most of his real estate in a short period, belatedly joining the policies of President Lee Jae-myung’s administration, deserves high praise. There aren’t many people like this." When PPP lawmakers brought up President Lee Jae-myung’s past comparison of multiple homeowners to "devils" and asked, "So, have you now turned from a devil into a human?" Han replied, "If you put it that way, I seem to have become human." When asked if he would invest in real estate if he returns to civilian life after serving as prime minister, Han said, "No, I won’t." <<> The confirmation hearing on this day proceeded without any witnesses or references, similar to the hearing for Prime Minister Kim Min-seok a year ago. PPP lawmaker Kang Seung-kyu (Chungnam Hongseong-Yesan), the secretary of the special committee on Han’s confirmation, remarked, "Is a hearing without witnesses the new normal? The National Assembly’s power to verify is being undermined." In response, DP lawmaker Kim Han-kyu (Jeju Jeju B), the committee secretary, argued, "We said we could accept most demands except for witnesses related to the Seongnam FC case, which would drag President Lee Jae-myung into a political battleground, but the PPP insisted all requested witnesses must be included." The ruling and opposition parties also clashed over the submission of documents. The PPP claimed that many requested documents from Han had not been submitted, while the DP countered, "Why would we need 30 years of blood donation records or high school grades?" Han’s confirmation hearing is set to continue until the 26th. (25일 열린 한성숙 국무총리 후보자 국회 인사청문회에선 한 후보자의 대북관과 부동산 처분 과정에 대한 질의가 쏟아졌다. 국민의힘은 네이버 대표 출신으로 중소벤처기업부 장관에 취임한 지 1년 만에 총리 후보자에 지명된 한 후보자의 외교·안보관을 파고들었다. 더불어민주당은 한 후보자가 청문회를 앞두고 보유 주택 4채 중 3채를 판 데 대해 “이런 분 잘 없다”며 “높이 평가해야 한다”고 했다. 이번 청문회는 여야 이견으로 증인과 참고인을 채택하지 못했는데, 국민의힘은 “민주당이 국회 인사 검증권을 무력화한다”고 했다.)

item.title: Lee: "Today's Peace and Prosperity Were Forged by the Sacrifices of Heroes" (李 “지금의 평화·번영, 영웅들 희생으로 일군 것”)
item.description:
Lee: "Today's Peace and Prosperity Were Forged by the Sacrifices of Heroes" (李 “지금의 평화·번영, 영웅들 희생으로 일군 것”)

President Lee Jae-myung attended the 76th anniversary ceremony of the Korean War on the 25th, stating, "The peace and prosperity we enjoy today were never achieved easily," and "They were built upon the noble sacrifices and dedication of heroes who gave everything they had and fought on the battlefields when the nation's fate hung by a thread." (이재명 대통령은 25일 6·25전쟁 76주년 기념식에 참석해 “지금 우리가 누리는 평화와 번영은 결코 거저 얻어진 것이 아니다”라며 “조국의 명운이 백척간두에 섰을 때 자신의 모든 것을 바쳐가며 전장을 누빈 영웅들의 고귀한 희생과 헌신으로 일궈진 것”이라고 했다.)

In his commemorative address at the ceremony held at the Suwon Convention Center, President Lee said, "On behalf of the people, I extend deep respect and gratitude to the veterans of the war," adding these remarks. Approximately 1,000 people, including veterans and their families, military officials, and foreign diplomatic envoys from allied nations, attended the ceremony that day. (이 대통령은 이날 수원컨벤션센터에서 열린 기념식에서 기념사를 통해 “국민을 대표해 참전 유공자 여러분께 깊은 존경과 감사의 말씀을 전한다”면서 이같이 말했다. 이날 기념식에는 유공자와 가족, 군 관계자와 참전국 외교사절 등 1000여명이 참석했다.)

President Lee emphasized, "It is our government's firm principle that special sacrifices and dedication for the nation must be met with special compensation and proper respect," and "We will do our utmost to ensure that the sacrifices of war veterans lead not merely to personal pride but to honorable and stable lives." On this day, the government awarded the Order of Military Merit, Chungmu, to the late veteran Kim Jang-seong, who had achieved distinguished service during the Korean War but fought as an irregular and had long been unrecognized, and the Order of Military Merit, Hwarang, to veteran Lee Young-bok and the late veteran Jeon Ha-jeong. (이 대통령은 “국가를 위한 특별한 희생과 헌신에는 특별한 보상과 마땅한 예우가 뒤따라야 한다는 것이 우리 정부의 확고한 원칙”이라며 “참전 용사의 희생이 개인 자부심에 그치지 않고 명예롭고 안정된 삶으로 이어질 수 있도록 최선을 다하겠다”고 했다. 이날 정부는 6·25 전쟁 때 전과를 올렸지만 비정규군으로 참전해 오랜 기간 공을 인정받지 못했던 고(故) 김장성 용사에게 충무무공훈장을, 이영복 용사와 고 전하정 용사에게 화랑무공훈장을 수여했다.)

Additionally, President Lee stated, "There are those we must never forget—the UN veterans," and "We will expand our veteran diplomacy, including invitations to visit Korea, to ensure that the spirit of solidarity born in the trenches lives on for future generations." (또 이 대통령은 “우리가 결코 잊지 말아야 할 분들이 있다. 바로 유엔 참전 용사들”이라며 “한국 방문 초청을 비롯한 보훈 외교를 더욱 확대해 참호 속에서 싹튼 연대의 정신이 미래 세대에도 살아 숨 쉴 수 있도록 더욱 노력할 것”이라고 말했다.)

President Lee also said, "I will steadfastly protect this great Republic of Korea built by heroes," and "With a strong defense capability, I will safeguard the people and the land and surely create a peaceful Korean Peninsula where there is no need to worry about war or fight." In his commemorative address that day, President Lee did not mention North Korea. (이 대통령은 “영웅들이 만든 이 위대한 대한민국을 흔들림 없이 지켜나가겠다”면서 “강력한 국방력으로 국민과 영토를 지키고 전쟁이 일어날 걱정도 싸울 필요도 없는 평화의 한반도를 반드시 만들어내겠다”고도 했다. 이 대통령은 이날 기념사에서 북한은 언급하지 않았다.)

At the subsequent reception for war veterans, President Lee remarked, "The reason the Republic of Korea has become a globally admired nation today is all thanks to your contributions." He noted that during foreign visits, he receives requests from heads of state for economic cooperation, such as semiconductors, and defense exports, and feels high regard for cultural and political aspects, adding, "This country was nearly destroyed, wasn't it?" "Thanks to those who dedicated their youth and lives in the Korean War, making sacrifices and commitments, the Republic of Korea has grown like this." (이어 열린 참전 유공자 위로연에서 이 대통령은 “대한민국이 오늘날 전 세계적으로 각광받는 나라가 된 것도 다 여러분들의 기여 덕분”이라고 했다. 외국 순방 중 각국 정상으로부터 반도체 등 경제 협력과 방산 수출을 요청받고 문화적·정치적 측면도 높은 평가를 받는 것을 체감한다면서 이 대통령은 “없어질 뻔한 나라 아니겠나” “6·25전쟁에서 청춘과 생명을 바쳐 헌신하고 희생하신 분들 덕분에 대한민국이 이렇게 성장했다”고 했다.)

item.title: As Opposition Party Convention Approaches… Kim Min-seok Says "Abolishing Supplementary Investigation Powers Is Government's Position" (與 전당대회 다가오자… 김민석 “보완수사권 폐지가 정부 입장”)
item.description:
As Opposition Party Convention Approaches… Kim Min-seok Says "Abolishing Supplementary Investigation Powers Is Government's Position" (與 전당대회 다가오자… 김민석 “보완수사권 폐지가 정부 입장”)

Prime Minister Kim Min-seok announced on the 25th that the government has finalized its basic stance as completely abolishing the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers without exceptions. He also stated that the government will not submit its own bill regarding the abolition of supplementary investigation powers to the National Assembly, leaving the matter to the legislature's discussion. With the August party convention to elect the next leadership of the Democratic Party approaching, hardliners like former party leader Jeong Cheong-rae, who is seeking re-election, have gained momentum with their "complete abolition of supplementary investigation powers" argument, leading the government to scrap internal discussions and follow the will of its staunch supporters. The People Power Party criticized, saying, "Is the race for party leadership more important than South Korea's criminal justice system? The Democratic Party is now running wild, looking only for the cheers of its hardcore supporters, not the people of South Korea." <<> At a press conference held at the Seoul Government Complex, Prime Minister Kim stated, "Considering the various opinions discussed and heard by the government, we have finalized the abolition of supplementary investigation powers as the government's basic position." He added, "The fundamental principle of prosecutorial reform promoted by President Lee Jae-myung's administration is the separation of investigation and prosecution. We will convey the government's basic position to the party, and thereafter, rather than the government proposing separate legislation, we will respect the discussions and decisions of the National Assembly." <<> The government established a Prosecutorial Reform Task Force under the Prime Minister's Office in October of last year and has been discussing revisions to the Criminal Procedure Act, including whether to retain the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers. The task force had nearly completed a draft of the government's proposal based on numerous public hearings and forums. However, with Prime Minister Kim's announcement that the government would not submit a separate bill to the National Assembly, the task force's discussions have effectively been nullified. It has been reported that neither the task force, the Ministry of Justice, nor the Supreme Prosecutors' Office were informed in advance of Kim's announcement. <<> There are interpretations that Kim's decision to hold an emergency press conference and announce the abolition of supplementary investigation powers is not unrelated to the competition for party leadership within the Democratic Party. President Lee had previously emphasized the need for exceptional supplementary investigation powers, stating, "Blocking even very exceptional cases could cause problems later." Similarly, Prime Minister Kim, during a press conference on the 22nd, had said, "A complete abolition is correct," while adding, "I fully understand President Lee's intentions," and called for deliberation. That Kim announced the "complete abolition of supplementary investigation powers" just three days later is seen as an intention not to fall behind in the race for clarity against former leader Jeong Cheong-rae, who has been emphasizing "full abolition of supplementary investigation powers" day after day. <<> It has been reported that Prime Minister Kim also discussed the press conference with President Lee. Senior Presidential Spokesperson Kang Yu-jeong said on the same day, "The prime minister's statement can be taken as a clarification of the government's position." The People Power Party commented, "What the government chose was neither the public's rights nor the stability of the criminal justice system. What it ultimately chose was the hardline stance of former leader Jeong, backed by his hardcore supporters." <<> Prime Minister Kim and former leader Jeong were also at odds that day. During the press conference, Kim attributed the delay in discussing the abolition of supplementary investigation powers to the opposition party's demands, saying, "We initially tried to expedite it and handle it in May, but it was postponed due to requests from the party ahead of local elections." In response, former leader Jeong shot back on Facebook, saying, "Not submitting the government bill? It makes one wonder if they've been wasting time for a year. I earnestly hope it's not some stalling tactic." He also called for completing legislation to abolish supplementary investigation powers before Constitution Day. <<> Within the legal community, there are criticisms that "the issue of the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers, which has a significant impact on people's lives, has become a sacrificial lamb in the fight for party leadership without proper deliberation." There are concerns that abolishing supplementary investigation powers without an alternative could worsen delays in investigations and eliminate the prosecution's ability to check police's inadequate investigations. A current senior prosecutor stated, "It's common sense among those experienced in investigation and trial practice that eliminating the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers would make it impossible to oversee the police's initial investigations." A lawyer who previously served as a deputy chief prosecutor also said, "Since the adjustment of investigative powers between the prosecution and police in 2021, case processing has been delayed, causing dissatisfaction among both crime victims and suspects. If even the prosecution's supplementary investigation powers are removed, the criminal justice system will not just face chaos but collapse." <<> According to the Ministry of Justice and the Supreme Prosecutors' Office, among 55,174 cases received by 12 prosecutors' offices nationwide in March and April, 45.59% (25,152 cases) involved supplementary investigations by the prosecution. These include cases such as a group sexual assault case that the police had decided not to forward to the prosecution, where the prosecution conducted supplementary investigations and detained the main perpetrator, and a case at a residential facility for severely disabled individuals where the prosecution identified additional rape offenses by the facility head. (김민석 국무총리는 검찰 보완수사권을 예외를 두지 않고 완전히 폐지하는 것을 정부의 기본 입장으로 정리했다고 25일 밝혔다. 또 보완수사권 폐지와 관련한 정부안을 국회에 제출하지 않고, 관련 논의를 국회에 일임하기로 했다. 민주당 차기 지도부를 뽑는 8월 전당대회를 앞두고 당대표 연임에 나서는 정청래 전 대표 등 강경파의 “보완수사권 완전 폐지” 주장이 힘을 얻자, 그간 정부 차원에서 이뤄진 논의를 폐기하고 강성 지지층 뜻에 따르겠다는 것이다. 국민의힘은 “당권 경쟁이 대한민국 형사사법 체계보다 더 중요한가”라며 “지금 민주당은 대한민국 국민이 아니라 ‘개딸’ 환호만 바라보며 폭주하고 있다”고 비판했다.)

item.title: Kim Min-seok and Chung Cheong-rae Head to 'Ruling Party Stronghold' North Jeolla (김민석·정청래 나란히 ‘與 텃밭’ 전북으로)
item.description:
Kim Min-seok and Chung Cheong-rae Head to 'Ruling Party Stronghold' North Jeolla (김민석·정청래 나란히 ‘與 텃밭’ 전북으로)

Kim Min-seok, Prime Minister and a contender for the leadership of the Democratic Party of Korea, along with former Democratic Party leader Chung Cheong-rae, visited the Honam region on the 25th. Honam is home to about one-third of the Democratic Party's paid members and is seen as a key battleground in the August Democratic Party leadership election. Another leadership contender, Democratic Party lawmaker Song Young-gil, is also expected to visit Honam soon. <<> Former leader Chung visited a workshop for elected officials hosted by the Democratic Party's North Jeolla Provincial Party in Jeongeup, North Jeolla, on the same day. Chung resigned from the Supreme Council the previous day, signaling his intent to seek another term, and chose North Jeolla as his first regional schedule after stepping down. North Jeolla is where, in the June 3 local gubernatorial election, pro-Chung candidate Lee Won-taek defeated independent candidate Kim Kwan-young to win. Chung emphasized, "For the first time in the history of local elections, Democratic Party candidates won in all 14 city and county basic local government heads. North Jeolla achieved a sweeping victory." <<> After the event, Chung met with reporters and commented on the timing of officially announcing his candidacy for party leader, saying, "There's a Western proverb: 'Make hay while the sun shines.' Everything has its time. A popular politician must always align with the public's sentiment. I'm carefully considering that aspect." This was interpreted as a statement that he would assess the direction of public opinion. <<> Prime Minister Kim also attended the same event that afternoon and delivered a congratulatory speech. However, their visit times differed, so they did not cross paths. Kim told reporters, "I want to play a role in setting the party's direction to rebuild the Democratic Party into a winning force. I'll have an opportunity to speak about the timing of my candidacy once I've returned to the party." On the 26th, Kim is scheduled to give a lecture in Gwangju to young people about former President Kim Dae-jung, fulfilling two consecutive days of Honam itinerary. <<> Democratic Party lawmaker Song Young-gil, who is currently on a business trip to the U.S., will return on the 27th and visit North Jeolla on the 28th. Song is expected to hold a town hall meeting in Jeonju and announce his stance on running in the party leadership election. While initial speculation suggested Song would only serve as a 'pacemaker' for Prime Minister Kim, recent indications suggest he may run the full race. A Democratic Party source said, "In Honam, the level of support for Song is surprisingly quite high." (더불어민주당 당권 주자로 꼽히는 김민석 국무총리와 정청래 전 민주당 대표가 25일 호남을 찾았다. 호남은 민주당 권리당원 약 3분의 1이 거주하는 지역으로 8월 민주당 당대표 선거에서도 주요 승부처로 꼽힌다. 또 다른 당권 주자인 송영길 민주당 의원도 곧 호남을 찾을 예정이다.)

item.title: Lee and Moon to Meet Ahead of Party Convention… Luncheon at the Blue House on July 1 (전대 앞두고 李·文 만난다… 내달 1일 靑 오찬)
item.description:
Lee and Moon to Meet Ahead of Party Convention… Luncheon at the Blue House on July 1 (전대 앞두고 李·文 만난다… 내달 1일 靑 오찬)

The Blue House announced on the 25th that President Lee Jae-myung will have a luncheon with former President Moon Jae-in at the Blue House on July 1. This marks the first solo meeting between President Lee and former President Moon since Lee took office. Blue House Senior Spokesperson Kang Yu-jung stated in a briefing, "They are meeting with an open agenda," adding, "They are expected to have a candid exchange of views on overall state affairs and the international situation." (이재명 대통령이 오는 7월 1일 청와대에서 문재인 전 대통령과 오찬을 한다고 청와대가 25일 밝혔다. 이 대통령이 취임 후 문 전 대통령과 단독 회동하는 것은 처음이다. 청와대 강유정 수석대변인은 브리핑에서 “(두 사람이) 열린 주제로 만나는 것”이라며 “국정 현안 전반과 국제 정세 관련해서 허심탄회하게 의견을 나눌 것으로 예상된다”고 했다.)

This meeting was arranged amid escalating conflict between the pro-Lee and pro-Moon factions ahead of the Democratic Party's convention to elect a new party leader in August. Recently, the pro-Lee and pro-Moon discord has intensified, spreading into a confrontation between the new mainstream 'New Lee Jae-myung' faction—supporting President Lee from around the last presidential election—and the old mainstream 'pro-Roh, pro-Moon' faction, deepening the rift within the ruling bloc. After former leader Jung Cheong-rae resigned his post and formally declared his bid for re-election the previous day, his meeting with former President Moon drew complaints from the pro-Lee camp, with some saying, "Isn't this a blatant expression of intent to rally the pro-Roh and pro-Moon forces and win?" (이번 만남은 오는 8월 민주당 당대표를 뽑는 전당대회를 앞두고 친명·친청 갈등이 격화하는 상황에서 성사됐다. 최근 친명·친청 갈등은 지난 대선 전후로 이 대통령을 지지하는 신주류 ‘뉴이재명’과 구주류 ‘친노·친문' 세력 간 대결로 번지면서 여권 분열이 심화되는 양상이었다. 전날 정청래 전 대표가 당대표직을 사퇴하며 연임 도전을 공식화한 뒤 문 전 대통령과 만난 것을 두고도 친명계에선 “친노·친문 세력을 결집해 이기겠다는 노골적 의지 표명 아니냐”는 불만이 나왔다.)

Following this, the Blue House's sudden scheduling of a luncheon with former President Moon has sparked various interpretations. It is said that the Blue House first proposed the meeting to Moon's side, and Moon accepted. A source within the ruling bloc commented, "While there may be an intention to resolve divisions within the support base, it could also be President Lee's way of supporting Prime Minister Kim Min-seok as a candidate for party leadership while keeping Jung in check." Pro-Moon key figure, Democratic Party lawmaker Yoon Gun-young, said on radio that day, "Former President Moon believes that for the success of the Lee Jae-myung administration, the party should resolve matters through unity and wisdom," adding, "In order to eliminate various rumors and misunderstandings, he intends to postpone all meetings with party leadership candidates until after the convention." (이후 청와대가 갑자기 문 전 대통령과의 오찬 일정을 잡자 여러 해석이 나왔다. 이 일정은 청와대가 문 전 대통령 측에 먼저 요청했고 문 전 대통령이 수락했다고 한다. 여권 관계자는 “지지층 분열을 해소하고자 하는 취지도 있겠으나, 이 대통령이 당권주자로 김민석 국무총리를 지원하고 정 전 대표를 견제하는 측면도 있지 않겠느냐”고 했다. 친문 핵심 윤건영 민주당 의원은 이날 라디오에서 “문 전 대통령은 이재명 정부의 성공을 위해 당이 통합과 단결 그리고 슬기롭게 해결했으면 좋겠다는 생각을 갖고 있다”며 “이런저런 설왕설래나 오해를 없앤다는 차원에서 당권 주자들과의 만남은 전당대회 이후로 다 미루려고 한다”고 했다.)

Meetings between President Lee and former President Moon have mostly occurred amid deepening divisions within the ruling bloc. When Lee was the Democratic Party leader in February 2024, ahead of the 22nd general election and as the 'anti-Lee's arbitrary purges' conflict grew, he visited former President Moon at Pyeongsan Village. In January 2025, during the presidential primary phase, as criticism of his one-person leadership intensified mainly from the anti-Lee faction, he again visited Pyeongsan Village. After taking office, he invited former President Moon and his wife to his inauguration—the National Appointment Ceremony—and met them at the 17th anniversary memorial service for the late former President Roh Moo-hyun on May 23, but this is the first time they are having a separate official meeting. (이 대통령과 문 전 대통령의 회동은 대부분 여권 내 분열이 심해지는 상황에서 이뤄졌다. 이 대통령은 민주당 대표 시절인 2024년 2월 22대 총선을 앞두고 ‘비명횡사’ 갈등이 커지자, 평산마을에서 문 전 대통령을 만났다. 2025년 1월 대선 경선 국면에서는 비명계를 중심으로 자신의 일극 체제에 대한 비판이 커지자 평산마을을 찾았다. 취임 후엔 취임식인 국민임명식에 문 전 대통령 부부를 초대했고, 지난달 23일 고(故) 노무현 전 대통령 서거 17주기 추도식에서 만난 적 있으나 별도의 공식 회동을 갖는 것은 이번이 처음이다.)

The Blue House reported that former President Moon's wife, Kim Jung-sook, will not attend due to overseas schedules. Consequently, President Lee's wife, Kim Hye-kyung, will also not be present at the luncheon. (문 전 대통령 부인 김정숙 여사는 해외 일정으로 인해 불참한다고 청와대는 전했다. 이에 따라 이 대통령 부인 김혜경 여사 역시 오찬에 참석하지 않는다.)

item.title: "I Feared Defeat More Than Death"... The Confession of Korea's First Four-Star General (“죽음보다 패전이 두려웠다”… 대한민국 최초 ‘4스타’ 장군의 고백)
item.description:
"I Feared Defeat More Than Death"... The Confession of Korea's First Four-Star General (“죽음보다 패전이 두려웠다”… 대한민국 최초 ‘4스타’ 장군의 고백)

At the former site of Seoul National University's College of Liberal Arts and Sciences in Dongsung-dong, Seoul, where the U.S. Eighth Army headquarters was located, then-U.S. President-elect Dwight Eisenhower eventually visited Gyeongmudae. This was the result of persuading Mark Clark, the United Nations Commander in Tokyo, who accompanied Eisenhower on his visit to Seoul. Following Clark's directive to "return to Gyeongmudae and wait," Army Chief of Staff Paik Sun-yup immediately got into a jeep and headed back to Gyeongmudae. President Syngman Rhee, who was eagerly hoping for his arrival, began preparations to welcome Eisenhower as soon as he heard Clark's words. Paik first inspected the military band stationed in the Gyeongmudae courtyard. <<> Around 6 o'clock, Eisenhower and his party arrived at Gyeongmudae. Eisenhower brought along his son, Major John Eisenhower, who was then serving in the war. The entourage included Clark, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Bradley, and the entire delegation visiting Korea. Eisenhower's party first held a brief honor guard review in the Gyeongmudae courtyard. They then moved to the reception room at Gyeongmudae and had a friendly conversation with President Syngman Rhee. With Eisenhower's son present, the atmosphere of the discussion was reportedly warm. <<> What if Eisenhower's visit to Gyeongmudae had ultimately fallen through? The relationship between the proud President Rhee and the U.S. administration could have become very strained. Many hurdles remained until the armistice was signed on July 27, 1953. If Eisenhower's failure to visit Gyeongmudae had further soured relations between the two governments, overcoming the numerous challenges ahead would have been much more difficult. <<> Paik Sun-yup's style, as revealed in resolving issues like Eisenhower's visit to Korea and subsequent friction with President Rhee, can be seen as highly multifaceted. He was generally known for his gentle demeanor. This was evident in his later years, long after the war ended. He showed utmost respect to everyone, regardless of age, and rarely changed his expression over trivial matters. His gentle expression and reluctance to boast about his exploits led some to ask, "Is that really our country's first four-star general?" <<> Paik Sun-yup himself said, "I tried to avoid quarreling with others over small matters as much as possible." He steered clear of verbal disputes and empty debates. When asked, "Weren't you afraid on the battlefield where life and death intersect?" he replied, "As a human, why wouldn't I have been afraid?" He added, "Nevertheless, as a soldier, I was prepared to risk my life when necessary." <<> Though undoubtedly a renowned commander, Paik Sun-yup was not the reckless type who would rush into battle without hesitation. This means that while courage is valuable on the battlefield where lives are at stake, he was not someone who decided outcomes based on that single virtue alone. He also seemed somewhat lacking in being called a wise general. He showed little interest in defeating opponents through strategy alone. This wasn't because he was the type to be overwhelmed by the enemy's momentum while solely focusing on finding methods and then retreating. Could he then be called a virtuous general? <<> His attitude toward subordinates was gentle and soft, but it didn't quite fit to label him solely as a virtuous general. To defeat the enemy, he was also a commander who, in the early morning, walked through frontline trenches, endlessly encouraging and urging his soldiers. Moreover, he was a commander who shunned the command room to avoid missing the battle situation, instead staying in the radio room, where the front-line updates came in directly, fighting off drowsiness. He was also not a virtuous general whose resolve could falter due to a tender heart before the enemy, overly concerned about conserving his troops. <<> Paik Sun-yup was a commander deeply immersed in war. Though his expression was gentle, it contained the determination he often spoke of: "I was not afraid of death, but I truly feared defeat." Thus, outwardly unassuming, inwardly he could be seen as a fierce competitor, gritting his teeth to defeat the opponent with a heart that felt like it was rotting away. With such qualities, he led the victory in the crucial battle for the nation—the Battle of Dabudong in Chilgok, Gyeongbuk. Driving through the arduous path of the northward advance, he led the significantly inferior 1st Division of the ROK Army in mobility and organization at the time to reach Pyongyang ahead of the U.S. 1st Cavalry Division. <<> He then showed bold decisiveness by ordering a retreat during a meeting engagement with Chinese forces, and as the vanguard of the ROK Army in recapturing Seoul from the Chinese, as the 1st Corps commander, he advanced the front northward. He served as the ROK's first armistice negotiation representative, succeeded in cleansing guerrilla forces around Jirisan, and took the first steps in modernizing the ROK Army through the re-establishment of the 2nd Corps, achieving numerous combat feats and accomplishments. The U.S. military often praised him, calling him "the most skillful leader" (as stated in a congratulatory letter from U.S. 1st Corps Commander Frank Milburn in April 1951 for Paik's promotion to 1st Corps commander). With such a record, Paik Sun-yup, at the age of 32, served as the Chief of Staff of the ROK Army. <<> This same Paik Sun-yup succeeded in turning around Eisenhower, who visited Korea as a president-elect but strenuously avoided visiting Gyeongmudae. He did this by resorting to a statement bordering on a threat: "How does the U.S. intend to manage an ROK military that will soon grow into a force of a million?" Through such deep contemplation and tenacious effort, he was soon to become Korea's first four-star general, with stars on his shoulders and forehead. <<> Eisenhower and his party safely began their return journey. The visit to Gyeongmudae took place, and in a harmonious atmosphere, Syngman Rhee and Eisenhower conversed. After they left, Paik Sun-yup was once again buried in his busy schedule, and accompanied President Rhee on his visit to Japan, arranged by Clark. U.S. military trust in Paik Sun-yup grew daily. However, Van Fleet, the commander of the U.S. Eighth Army, who had astonishingly devoted himself to strengthening the ROK military in less than two years since his arrival on the Korean front, was soon to depart. <<> Maxwell Taylor, who had led the initial assault in the Normandy landings, was about to take command of the new U.S. Eighth Army. As Van Fleet, who had diligently aided Korea, stepped down, the situation could face considerable changes. Then, one day, as Paik Sun-yup sat in his office at the ROK Army headquarters in Daegu, he saw his secretaries preparing something outside his office door. Soon, a message arrived from the temporary Gyeongmudae in Busan. It said, "Report to Gyeongmudae." <<>> (서울 동숭동 옛 서울대 문리대 자리에 있던 미8군 사령부에서 드와이트 아이젠하워 당시 미 대통령 차기 당선자는 결국 경무대를 예방했다. 아이젠하워 당선자를 수행해 서울에 함께 왔던 도쿄 주재 유엔군 총사령관 마크 클라크를 설득한 결과였다. “경무대로 돌아가 기다려라”고 했던 클라크의 언질에 따라 백선엽 육군 참모총장은 곧장 지프에 올라타 경무대로 돌아왔다. 그가 오길 간절히 기대하고 있던 이승만 대통령은 클라크의 발언을 전하자 곧장 아이젠하워를 맞이할 준비에 들어갔다. 백선엽은 경무대 뜰에 있던 군악대를 우선 점검했다.)

item.title: [Exclusive] Following the ROK Army Academy Alumni Association, the Naval and Air Force Academy Alumni Associations Also "Oppose the Hasty Integration" ([단독] 육사 총동창회 이어 해·공사 총동창회도 “졸속 통합에 반대”)
item.description:
As the Ministry of National Defense pushes forward with a plan to merge the Army, Navy, and Air Force academies into a single "Republic of Korea Armed Forces Academy," it was learned on the 25th that the alumni associations of the Navy and Air Force academies have joined the Army Academy Alumni Association in declaring their opposition to the "hasty integration." The merger of the military academies is a campaign pledge of President Lee Jae-myung. (국방부가 육·해·공군 사관학교를 합쳐 ‘국군사관학교’로 만드는 통합안을 추진 중인 가운데, 육군사관학교 총동창회에 이어 해·공군 사관학교 총동창회까지 ‘졸속 통합에 반대한다’는 입장을 정한 것으로 25일 알려졌다. 사관학교 통합은 이재명 대통령의 대선 공약이다.)

According to this newspaper's reporting, Park Pan-joon, chairman of the ROK Army Academy Alumni Association (retired colonel); Lee Beom-rim, chairman of the ROK Naval Academy Alumni Association (retired lieutenant general); and Hwang Seong-jin, chairman of the ROK Air Force Academy Alumni Association (retired lieutenant general), recently met and reportedly resolved to "oppose the government's hasty push for the integrated military academy as a unified front." They also agreed to issue any future statements jointly under the names of all three alumni associations and to share related materials in real time. (본지 취재에 따르면, 박판준 육사 총동창회장(예비역 대령)과 이범림 해사 총동창회장(예비역 중장), 황성진 공사 총동창회장(예비역 중장)은 최근 만나 ‘정부의 통합 사관학교 졸속 추진을 단일 대오로 반대한다’는 결의를 한 것으로 알려졌다. 향후 관련 입장문을 낼 때도 총동창회 3곳의 공동 명의로 하고, 통합 관련 자료도 실시간 공유하기로 했다.)

Earlier, on the 16th, the Army Academy Alumni Association issued a statement demanding a "return to square one" for the integration plan, stating that "the Ministry of National Defense is pursuing the merger without objective research, military scientific verification, or sincere communication." Now, the Naval and Air Force academy alumni associations have also stepped in to put the brakes on the plan. (앞서 육사 총동창회는 지난 16일 입장문을 내고 사관학교 통합안에 대해 “국방부는 객관적인 연구나 군사학적 검증, 진지한 소통을 결여한 채 통폐합을 추진하고 있다”며 ‘원점 재검토’를 요구했다. 여기에 해·공사 총동창회까지 제동을 걸고 나선 것이다.)

The Ministry of National Defense is expected to unveil the specific details of the academy integration plan as early as next month. It has been reported that they are considering a "2+2 format" integration model, where first- and second-year students at the Armed Forces Academy would receive common foundational training together, while third- and fourth-year students would split into the Army, Navy, and Air Force for advanced specialized courses. Although the intention is to strengthen joint operations education, concerns are emerging both within and outside the military that this "could undermine the expertise of each service." (국방부는 구체적인 사관학교 통합안을 이르면 다음 달쯤 공개할 예정인데 국군사관학교 1~2학년은 공통 기초 소양을 같이 교육받고, 3~4학년은 육·해·공군을 나눠 전공 심화 과정을 다루는 ‘2+2 방식’ 통합을 구상하고 있는 것으로 전해졌다. 합동성 교육을 강화한다는 취지지만, 군 안팎에선 “각 군의 전문성을 해칠 수 있다”는 우려가 나온다.)

Lee Beom-rim, a former commander of the Naval Education and Training Command and superintendent of the Naval Academy, told this newspaper in a phone interview, "Jointness is an issue that comes only after expertise in one's own service is firmly established," adding, "It is difficult to cultivate competent Navy officers specializing in the advanced courses within just two years in the third and fourth years." Hwang Seong-jin, a former commander of the Air Force Operations Command and superintendent of the Air Force Academy, also commented, "Merging the academies risks deepening uniform groupthink, and establishing a new liberal arts college to handle first- and second-year students would be inefficient in terms of both budget and personnel management." (해군교육사령관과 해군사관학교장을 지낸 이범림 회장은 본지 통화에서 “합동성은 자군에 대한 전문성이 일단 갖춰진 다음의 문제”라며 “3~4학년 2년 안에 전문성 있는 해군 장교를 키워내긴 어렵다”고 했다. 공군작전사령관과 공군사관학교장을 지낸 황성진 회장도 “사관학교를 합치면 획일화된 집단 사고(思考)가 심화될 우려가 있고, 1~2학년을 담당하는 교양 대학을 신설하는 것도 예산·인력 운영 면에서 비효율적”이라고 했다.)

Meanwhile, as of today, over 70,000 people have agreed to a petition posted on the National Assembly's electronic petition website calling for the halt of the military academy merger. If the number of supporters exceeds 50,000, the relevant standing committee of the National Assembly will take up the petition. (한편, 국회 전자청원 홈페이지에 ‘사관학교 통폐합을 중단해달라’는 취지로 올라온 청원에는 이날까지 7만명 이상이 동의했다. 동의한 사람이 5만명 이상이면 관련 국회 상임위에서 해당 청원을 다룬다.)
